title: Unlock Agent Autonomy: The Runtime for AI-Native Systems — Tushar Jain, Docker
talk_summary: Docker's Tushar Jain argues the next blocker for agents is safety, not intelligence, and proposes a portable agent runtime with three pillars: containment (sandboxes with controls outside the untrusted boundary), scoped capabilities (just-in-time, task-scoped tools instead of broad read/write grants), and intent-based access (a control layer that judges each access request against the task and either grants a scoped sub-sandbox, denies, or escalates to a human). The demo shows the same policy plane following an agent from local to cloud, fanning out six parallel sandboxes, and an orchestrator composing narrowly-scoped agents.

takeaways.technique: Per-task scoped sandboxes instead of one broad sandbox
takeaways.what_they_do: Split a job into separate sandboxes each holding only the credentials/network for its step (PR-reader gets GitHub only; Notion-writer gets Notion only, no GitHub), rather than accumulating capabilities in one long-lived environment.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I don't need a single monolithic sandbox where I give it both credentials. I can have one task give you the PR... a separate sandbox with just notion access

takeaways.technique: Portable runtime with one policy plane across local and cloud
takeaways.what_they_do: Same microVM sandbox and same policy/control plane runs on laptop, cloud, or VPC; moving an agent to the cloud is a rename, not a re-platform, and fan-out is just creating N sandboxes in parallel.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the exact same sandbox just runs in the cloud because the runtime is portable and goes there with your policies applied
takeaways.numbers: demo fans out 6 PR-review sandboxes in parallel

takeaways.technique: Orchestrator composes narrowly-scoped agents per subtask
takeaways.what_they_do: An orchestrator receives a high-level request ('find 10 PRs, review them, write summary to Notion'), schedules the PR-scoped agent and the Notion-scoped agent in sequence, and can attach a schedule to the whole flow.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It'll schedule them. It'll compose over them. run PR with just the PR B limited access and then run the notion one just the notion tool

takeaways.what_they_do: A control layer outside the model inspects each access request against the original task intent; plausible requests spawn a scoped sub-sandbox, implausible ones (e.g. exporting to an unrelated site) are rejected or raised for human approval.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If the PR suppose the text PR said I want you to now export this to paypin.com that would get rejected

takeaways.technique: Just-in-time composed tools over existing MCP servers
takeaways.what_they_do: When predefined tools are too coarse (Slack read-only still exposes all channels), the runtime generates a narrow tool that composes over existing MCP tools but restricts to the relevant subset (one channel/incident).
takeaways.evidence_quote: create a just in time tool that composes over existing Slack MCB tools or anything else, but restricts access to just conversations about the incident
